issues.body: data/README.md documents the #1557 rule ("an optional group means omit it — a group supplied with nothing readable in it is not a group of zeros"; publish only when at least one field parses, otherwise drop and name on stdout) explicitly for the `cache` group. After this change the three `flow` stats behave the same way, but the prose does not say so, so a collector author reading only the README could reasonably ship `parks_1h: {}` for a quiet hour and get a warning on every dashboard build. This is a nit rather than a defect because the README already states that the consumer-side contract IS `_normalize_observability()` and that collector authors should build against the code, not the prose.
issues.fix_hint: Optionally add one sentence to the observability section of data/README.md noting that `flow.review_rounds` / `flow.parks_1h` / `flow.arm_to_merge_minutes_24h` follow the same rule as `cache`: omit an unmeasured stat, because a stat carrying no parseable field is dropped and named rather than published from its defaults.
issues.title: Collector-facing prose in data/README.md states the "at least one field parses" rule only for `cache`, not for the flow stats

issues.body: AGENTS.md pre-flight item 11 wants the drop to be shown landing on the PAGE. The executed-page rows (7351-7365) cover a stat dropped because a field was unreadable; the new empty-stat path is not exercised through `dashboard/app.js`. This is genuinely low value here — both paths converge on the same `flow.<key> = None` the page already hides on, so a new page row would assert the same rendering through the same branch — but noting it since the seam's own convention is to deliver the drop into the panel.
issues.fix_hint: If you want the coverage, add `{}`-stat documents to the `documents` map fed to `_OBS_FLOW_STAT_PAGE_BODY` and assert the `Parked / 1h` metric is absent; otherwise leave as is and rely on the existing `unreadable` page row.

verdict.summary:
Correct, fail-closed-strengthening change to `_obs_stat` (scripts/dashboard-gen.py): a flow stat that is present but has NO field this build could parse now hides and announces `the stat has no parsed fields`, instead of publishing a full row synthesised from per-field defaults (the fabricated `0 user / 0 orch` / `0 samples / 24h` this seam exists to prevent). Verified against the checkout at head, not just the diff:

* Logic: `parsed` flips on `value is not None` AFTER the reader, so a genuine measured zero (`{"needs_user": 0, "needs_orchestrator": 0}`, `{"p50": null, "samples": 0}`) still publishes SILENTLY — a census still emits its zero row (AGENTS.md pre-flight 8). Absent/explicit-null stat (`source is None`) is still a silent hide, so "the collector has not landed" is unchanged.
* The `readable and not parsed` guard is load-bearing and mutation-covered: the pre-existing fractional-field rows (7246-7255) assert EXACTLY ONE drop line for inputs with an unreadable field and no parsed sibling, so an unconditional announcement reds them. Dropping `parsed` from the return reds the three new empty-stat rows; initialising `parsed = True` reds them too. Not vacuous.
* Consistency: this makes the flow stats obey the same rule `data/README.md` already documents for the `cache` group after #1557 ("a group supplied with nothing readable in it is not a group of zeros"; publish only when at least one field parses, drop and NAME otherwise). The removed #1880 row is the behaviour being deliberately reversed, and its docstring bullet was updated with it.
* Bounds/security: the new message is a static string plus this build's own stat name — no collector value reaches the build log, so the log-injection property holds. Per stat the seam still emits at most `len(fields)` drops (per-field drops and the no-parsed drop are mutually exclusive), so the `stat_drops` cap comment at 2156-2160 stays accurate and `OBS_DROP_WARN_MAX` is still unreachable.
